group: Who has borrowed by selling bonds
title: Who has borrowed abroad by selling bonds, by the borrower's nationality: international debt securities outstanding, in US dollars

rows.name: Not assigned to a country
rows.basis: the BIS world total minus every country and international organisations (our calculation)

source: Bank for International Settlements, international debt securities (WS_DEBT_SEC2_PUB 1.0), amounts outstanding, all currencies, US dollars, by the borrower's nationality, quarterly from December 1962
note: International debt securities are bonds and notes a borrower sells outside its home market, for example a dollar bond that a Brazilian company sells in London. Each amount is what is still owed, in US dollars at the BIS's rate, so a row can move with exchange rates without any borrowing or repaying. A borrower's nationality is where its parent is based, so a Chinese company's Hong Kong subsidiary counts as China. Not assigned is the BIS world total minus every country and international organisations: 0.034% of the total in the latest quarter, at most 0.119% since 2000, and up to 3.8% in 1986. A country whose row stops has nothing outstanding the BIS reports after that quarter, and its row says so. Source: Bank for International Settlements.
